newsitem.title: UK: DHL pinpoints Airbus Europe freight route.
newsitem.headline: DHL pinpoints Airbus Europe freight route.

text.p: DHL Worldwide Express said it hopes to be operating two converted Airbus A300B4 freighters on routes linking Scandinavia, the UK, Iberia and possibly Istanbul and Greece with Brussels in the last quarter of 1997.
Gordon Olafson, managing director of DHL sister company European Air Transport (EAT), said in a telephone from Brussels that a number of leasing possibilities were currently being evaluated.

Among the leasing options, he said, were two former EgyptAir A300s now being converted into 45 tonne capacity freighters at Dresden for U.S. leasing company Pinnacle, and up to 13 conversion orders for the aircraft type negotiated by U.S. lessor C-S Aviation Services with British Aerospace Plc (BAe).

Additionally, said Olafson -- whose EAT is responsible for providing DHL with night-time European freighter capacity -- UK carrier Channel Express was expecting to introduce its first Bae converted A300 freighter into service in May.
This has been contracted by British Airways to operate twice-weekly London-Tel Aviv services.

"It will only be operating for BA during the day. We have been talking with Channel Express and it may be available for us overnight. They are expecting delivery of a second A300 freighter by the end of this year," said Olafson.
He also said that DHL would also be buying four ex-Ansett Boeing 727s by the end of this year, for conversion into freighters.

DHL currently flies some 50 aircraft in its European network, including two DC-8s (respectively wet-leased from Emery Worldwide and Southern Air Transport), which operate five-times-weekly-weekly Stockholm-Copenhagen-Brussels and a daily Brussels-Spain one-way service.
Wet-leasing covers the hire of both aircraft and crew.

A leased Boeing 757 freighter flies six-times-a-week between Bahrain-Brussels and the remainder of the European freighter fleet comprises 25 727-100s and -200s, 10 Lockheed Electras, nine Convairs and, linking Ljubljana, Sofia and Bucharest with Budapest and Nuremburg, Antonov AN-26s and Czech-built LET-410s.
"The A300s, if and when we get them, will take over from the DC-8s and we may see some of the (older) 727s fall out as well," Olafson said.
